Class ArchiveSource

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.ArchiveSource
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class ArchiveSource extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Random access to the bytes of the outer runner archive.

By default the whole file is mapped once with FileChannel.map(FileChannel.MapMode, long, long, Arena) into a MemorySegment owned by a shared Arena, so that reading an entry costs a page fault at worst and never a system call, and so that defining a class from a STORED entry can hand the VM a ByteBuffer view instead of a copy. Every accessor takes an absolute offset in the outer file, which is exactly what the index stores, so no per-entry bookkeeping is needed.

Setting the system property "micronaut.runner.mmap" to exactly "false" selects a fallback mode that maps nothing and serves every read with a positional FileChannel.read(ByteBuffer, long) into a heap buffer. The fallback exists for platforms or containers where a large mapping is unwelcome; it is behaviourally identical, only slower, and the same tests run against both modes.

Lifetime

The instance is AutoCloseable, but the launcher never closes it: application threads keep loading classes for as long as the JVM lives, so the mapping must outlive main. Tests and benchmarks do close it, and they must: on Windows an open mapping prevents the file from being deleted. close() closes the arena, which invalidates the segment, and then the channel.

Truncation

A memory mapping is a view of the file as it is now. If the archive is truncated or replaced in place while it is mapped, touching a page that no longer exists raises SIGBUS, which the JVM reports as a fatal error that no Java code can catch. That is why the index carries the file length (IndexFormat.H_OUTER_FILE_LENGTH) and the local header signature of every nested jar: both are cheap staleness checks that turn "the jar was rebuilt or edited underneath us" into a clear IllegalStateException before any stale offset is dereferenced.

Thread safety

Everything after open(File) is safe for concurrent use by any number of class-loading threads: the segment is immutable, positional channel reads do not touch the channel position, and the inflater pool is guarded by its own lock. Only close() must not race with readers.

    • MAX_SLICE_LENGTH

      public static final int MAX_SLICE_LENGTH
      Largest slice slice(long, int) can produce. MemorySegment.asByteBuffer() only supports segments up to Integer.MAX_VALUE bytes, and array allocation is capped a little below that on most VMs, so larger entries have to be streamed by stream(long, long, long, int).

    • open

      public static ArchiveSource open(File file) throws IOException
      Opens an archive for reading.

      Nothing about the content is checked here: an archive that is not a runner jar, or not a ZIP file at all, is only diagnosed by openIndex(), so that the primitives stay usable over any file.

      Parameters:
      file - the outer archive, which must exist and be readable
      Returns:
      an open source, mapped unless "micronaut.runner.mmap" is "false"
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be opened or cannot be mapped

    • slice

      public ByteBuffer slice(long offset, int length) throws IOException
      A read-only view of a region of the archive. In the mapped mode this copies nothing: the buffer is a window onto the mapping, which is what lets the class loader define a STORED class without ever materialising a byte[]. In the fallback mode the region is read into a heap array first.

      The returned buffer's byte order is the ByteBuffer default, big-endian; callers reading little-endian structures out of it must set the order themselves.

      Parameters:
      offset - absolute offset in the archive
      length - number of bytes, at most MAX_SLICE_LENGTH
      Returns:
      a read-only buffer positioned at zero with the region as its content
      Throws:
      IOException - if the region is outside the archive, the length is negative or too large, or the read fails

    • stream

      public InputStream stream(long dataOffset, long compressedSize, long uncompressedSize, int method) throws IOException
      Streams the content of an entry, decompressing it when needed.

      The stream delivers exactly uncompressedSize bytes and then reports end of input. Fewer bytes (a truncated archive or a truncated deflate stream) and more bytes (data that does not match the recorded size) both raise an IOException, because either means the archive no longer agrees with the index. Entries larger than MAX_SLICE_LENGTH, which slice(long, int) cannot cover, stream correctly: the region is read in chunks.

      Parameters:
      dataOffset - absolute offset of the entry data, that is, past its local file header
      compressedSize - number of stored bytes
      uncompressedSize - number of bytes the caller must see
      method - IndexFormat.METHOD_STORED or IndexFormat.METHOD_DEFLATED
      Returns:
      a stream over the entry content, which the caller closes
      Throws:
      IOException - if the region is outside the archive, the sizes disagree for a STORED entry, or the method is not supported

    • inflate

      public byte[] inflate(long dataOffset, int compressedSize, int uncompressedSize) throws IOException
      Decompresses a DEFLATE entry into an array of exactly uncompressedSize bytes.

      This is the class loading path for a compressed archive, so it allocates one array, borrows an inflater from the pool and, in the mapped mode, feeds the inflater a direct buffer over the mapping rather than copying the compressed bytes first.

      Parameters:
      dataOffset - absolute offset of the entry data
      compressedSize - number of stored bytes
      uncompressedSize - number of bytes the entry expands to
      Returns:
      the decompressed content
      Throws:
      IOException - if the deflate stream is corrupt, ends early, produces more than uncompressedSize bytes, or does not consume all compressedSize bytes

    • openIndex

      public long[] openIndex() throws IOException
      Locates MICRONAUT-INF/index.bin in the outer archive without java.util.zip.

      The end of central directory record is found by scanning back from the end of the file, following the ZIP64 locator when one sits immediately before it, falling back to the 32-bit fields when the entry count carries the 0xFFFF marker but no locator does, and the central directory is then walked until the index entry is found. By construction it is the second entry, right after the manifest, so this reads a couple of records. The entry's true data offset comes from its local header, whose name and extra field lengths may differ from the central directory's.

      Returns:
      a two element array: the absolute offset of the index data and its length in bytes
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file is not a ZIP archive, carries no index, or the archive disagrees with itself
